title: 24-Layer Widened Initialization UV-SWIR Dual-Band Filter
scientific_hypothesis: Increasing layer count from 16 to 24 while applying widened initialization envelope (odd layers 20-40 nm, even layers 80-110 nm) with 5% periodic scaling perturbation will improve dual-band spectral separation by providing additional degrees of freedom for optimization without exceeding the 30-layer manufacturing constraint.
design_principle: Non-quarter-wave thickness optimization with expanded search space enables better trade-off between UV reflection band (200-400 nm) and SWIR transmission band (800-1500 nm). Widened initialization forces stronger departure from quarter-wave symmetry to accelerate convergence toward extended-bandwidth solutions.
proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
design_variables: Initial thickness bounds: odd positions 20-40 nm, even positions 80-110 nm
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 800-1500 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 200-400 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: HfO2 and SiO2 only (material constraint satisfied)
Thickness bounds ensure fabricable layer thicknesses
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer interference
Widened initialization envelope per feedback directives
expected_advantages: Improved spectral separation between UV and SWIR bands
More thickness degrees of freedom for optimization
known_risks: Increased computational cost with more layers
Potential for local minima in larger search space
May not improve if 16 layers already near-optimal for this material pair
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 multilayer stack on fused silica substrate for dual-band performance. Layer sequence: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Initialize odd-layer positions (1,3,5,...,23) with random thickness between 20-40 nm. Initialize even-layer positions (2,4,6,...,24) with random thickness between 80-110 nm. Apply 5% periodic scaling perturbation to initial stack. Optimize all 24 layer thicknesses using gradient-based optimizer with evolutionary initialization. Evaluate performance at normal incidence, unpolarized light. Compute target score based on: maximize transmittance in 800-1500 nm band, maximize reflectance in 200-400 nm band. Total layer count fixed at 24. Materials: HfO2 (high index), SiO2 (low index). Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 200-400 nm, 800-1500 nm. soft objectives: High transmission in 800-1500 nm band; High reflection in 200-400 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low transmission in 200-400 nm band; Low reflection in 800-1500 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Total layers <= 30; Materials limited to HfO2 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Increased layer count from 16 to 24 per feedback directive to widen initialization envelope and provide additional optimization degrees of freedom. Applied specified initialization bounds (odd 20-40 nm, even 80-110 nm) and 5% periodic scaling perturbation to force stronger departure from quarter-wave symmetry.
